• The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) scheme focuses on providing financial assistance for product trials, prototype development, and market entry. Skill development is not a primary objective of this scheme.

Further Insight:

• Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)

• Launch Date: April 1, 2021

• Aim: Provide financial assistance to startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry, and commercialization.

• Main Features:

○ Targets startups in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

○ Maximum grant: ₹50 lakh per startup.

○ Objective: Strengthen the startup ecosystem in India, reduce the risk at the idea stage, and create job opportunities.

• The Ayushman Sahakar Scheme is designed to assist cooperatives in setting up healthcare facilities and infrastructure.

Further Insight:

• Ayushman Sahakar Scheme

• Launch Date: October 19, 2020

• Aim: Assist cooperatives in setting up healthcare infrastructure.

• Main Features:

○ Financing by National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC).

○ Targets rural healthcare systems and cooperative hospitals.

○ Provides loans up to ₹10,000 crore.

○ Encourages cooperatives to establish hospitals and medical education institutions.

• The Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS) component of PM AASHA provides payments to farmers to cover the gap between the market price and the Minimum Support Price (MSP).

• PSS focuses on physical procurement.

• PPSS involves private procurement.

• MIS is not a part of PM AASHA.

Further Insight:

• Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan (PM AASHA)

• Launch Date: September 2018

• Aim: Provide remunerative prices to farmers for their produce.

• Main Features:

○ Components: Price Support Scheme (PSS), Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS), Pilot Private Procurement & Stockist Scheme (PPSS).

○ Focuses on procurement of pulses, oilseeds, and copra.

○ Supports farmers by ensuring MSP (Minimum Support Price) payments.

• Mission Sagar focuses on providing medical and logistical aid to countries in the Indian Ocean Region, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Further Insight:

• Mission Sagar

• Launch Date: May 2020

• Aim: Strengthen ties with Indian Ocean Region (IOR) countries during crises, particularly COVID-19.

• Main Features:

○ Part of India's maritime diplomacy initiative.

○ Provides medical supplies and humanitarian aid to Indian Ocean countries (like Maldives, Seychelles, and Mauritius).

○ Reflects India's policy of Security and Growth for All in the Region (SAGAR).

• The NIRVIK Scheme focuses on insurance coverage and simplifying credit, but it does not offer direct capital subsidies.

Further Insight:

• NIRVIK Scheme (Niryat Rin Vikas Yojana)

• Launch Date: February 1, 2020

• Aim: Improve export credit availability and provide insurance to exporters.

• Main Features:

○ Provides insurance coverage up to 90% of the loan amount.

○ Reduces insurance premium rates for small exporters.

○ Ensures quicker and easier loan disbursal to exporters.

○ Focus on promoting Indian exports globally.

• SVAMITVA aims to provide villagers with clear ownership records of their land using modern technology such as drones.

Further Insight:

• SVAMITVA Scheme (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas)

• Launch Date: April 24, 2020

• Aim: Provide property ownership records in rural areas through drone technology.

• Main Features:

○ Helps in mapping rural properties and providing clear ownership titles.

○ Promotes financial inclusion by enabling villagers to use property as collateral.

○ Aims at reducing land disputes.

○ Joint initiative of Ministry of Panchayati Raj and state governments.

• National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) focuses on technical textiles, not traditional textile exports.

Further Insight:

• National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM)

• Launch Date: February 26, 2020

• Aim: Promote the use and production of technical textiles in India.

• Main Features:

○ Four-year mission (2020-2024) with a budget of ₹1,480 crore.

○ Focus on R&D, product development, and market promotion of technical textiles.

○ Aims to position India as a global leader in technical textiles.

• DHRUV identifies talented children and nurtures them in science and performing arts.

Further Insight:

• DHRUV - PM Innovative Learning Programme

• Launch Date: October 10, 2019

• Aim: Identify and nurture talented children in the fields of science and performing arts.

• Main Features:

○ Provides advanced learning opportunities for high-performing students.

○ Focuses on holistic development through mentorship and exposure to innovation.

• The SERB-POWER scheme is designed to support women scientists and promote opportunities for them in research fields.

Further Insight:

• SERB-POWER Scheme (Promoting Opportunities for Women in Exploratory Research)

• Launch Date: October 29, 2020

• Aim: Promote and empower women in scientific research.

• Main Features:

○ Supports research funding for women scientists.

○ Provides two categories of research grants (SERB-POWER Fellowship and SERB-POWER Research Grants).

○ Encourages greater participation of women in research leadership positions.

• The One Nation One Ration Card Scheme (ONORCS) enables beneficiaries to access their ration entitlements across India, regardless of where they are.

Further Insight:

• One Nation One Ration Card Scheme (ONORCS)

• Launch Date: Implemented in phases since 2019

• Aim: Ensure nationwide portability of ration cards under the Public Distribution System (PDS).

• Main Features:

○ Allows beneficiaries to claim their entitled food grains from anywhere in India.

○ Especially beneficial for migrant workers.

○ Integrated with Aadhaar to ensure transparency and reduce leakages.

• PM SVANidhi Scheme offers collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors to help them restart their businesses after the COVID-19 lockdowns.

Further Insight:

• PM SVANidhi (Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi)

• Launch Date: June 1, 2020

• Aim: Provide working capital loans to street vendors for post-COVID-19 recovery.

• Main Features:

○ Collateral-free loan of up to ₹10,000.

○ Encourages digital transactions by offering cashback.

○ Enables street vendors to restart their businesses affected by the pandemic.

• Mission Karmayogi focuses on the capacity building of civil servants through competency-driven learning and upskilling.

Further Insight:

• Mission Karmayogi

• Launch Date: September 2, 2020

• Aim: Transform the civil services in India through capacity building.

• Main Features:

○ Focuses on upskilling civil servants through digital learning platforms.

○ Involves performance management and leadership development.

○ National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) is part of the initiative.

• The scheme is aimed at offering internships to young professionals to help them gain experience in the cooperative sector.

Further Insight:

• Sahakar Mitra Scheme

• Launch Date: June 12, 2020

• Aim: Provide internships to young professionals in cooperatives.

• Main Features:

○ Offers hands-on experience in the cooperative sector.

○ Internship program supported by the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC).

○ Helps youth develop leadership and managerial skills within cooperatives.

• Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana(PMVVY) offers a guaranteed pension but the pension amount depends on the investment, not a fixed ₹3,000.

Further Insight:

• Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY)

• Launch Date: May 4, 2017

• Aim: Provide a guaranteed pension to senior citizens.

• Main Features:

○ Fixed pension for individuals aged 60 years and above.

○ Maximum purchase price: ₹15 lakh.

○ Policy term: 10 years, with an assured return of 7.4% per annum.

• The scheme aims at strengthening domestic industries and making India self-reliant in production, agriculture, and healthcare.

Further Insight:

• Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan

• Launch Date: May 2020 (Economic stimulus package in response to COVID-19)

• Aim: Make India self-reliant in production and economic activities.

• Main Features:

○ ₹20 lakh crore stimulus package.

○ Focus on MSMEs, agriculture, defense, and healthcare.

○ Five pillars: Economy, Infrastructure, System, Vibrant Demography, and Demand.

• The Samarth Scheme focuses on capacity building in the textile sector by providing skill development training.

Further Insight:

• Samarth Scheme

• Launch Date: Launched under the Skill India Mission

• Aim: Provide skill development and capacity building in the textile sector.

• Main Features:

○ Targets youth and women workers in the textile industry.

○ Provides employment-oriented training programs.

○ Aims to boost production and productivity in textile manufacturing.

• Rashtriya Gokul Mission is focused on conserving and promoting the indigenous breeds of cattle in India.

Further Insight:

• Rashtriya Gokul Mission

• Launch Date: December 16, 2014

• Aim: Promote the conservation and development of indigenous cattle breeds.

• Main Features:

○ Focuses on genetic improvement of indigenous breeds.

○ Establishment of Gokul Grams (cattle development centers).

○ Aims to improve milk production and enhance farmers' incomes.

• PM FME (Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises) Scheme focuses on micro food processing enterprises, not large industries.

Further Insight:

• PM FME (Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme)

• Launch Date: June 29, 2020

• Aim: Formalize micro food processing units and increase their productivity.

• Main Features:

○ Offers financial, technical, and business support to micro-enterprises.

○ Focus on clusters and groups (such as Self-Help Groups and Farmer Producer Organizations).

○ Target: 2 lakh micro food processing units.

• The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) aims to double fish production and fishers' income by 2024-25 through sustainable fishery practices.

Further Insight:

• Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)

• Launch Date: September 10, 2020

• Aim: Enhance fish production and double the income of fish farmers by 2024-25.

• Main Features:

○ Total outlay of ₹20,050 crore, the largest investment in the fisheries sector.

○ Focus on sustainable aquaculture, processing, and value addition.

○ Target: Increasing fish production by an additional 70 lakh tonnes by 2024-25.

• KUSUM (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan) Scheme focuses on installing solar pumps and promoting renewable energy for agricultural irrigation.

Further Insight:

• KUSUM (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan)

• Launch Date: February 19, 2019 (Approval Date)

• Aim: Promote the use of solar energy in agriculture, particularly for irrigation.

• Main Features:

○ Installation of solar pumps for irrigation.

○ Encourage farmers to set up grid-connected solar power plants.

○ Target: 30.8 GW of solar power capacity by 2022.
